translations.text: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and Timothy our brother, to the church of God in Corinth, together with all the saints throughout Achaia.
Grace to you and peace from God our Father and from the Lord Jesus Christ.
Blessed is the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies and the God of all comfort,
who comforts us in all our troubles, so that we can comfort those who are in any trouble with the comfort with which we ourselves are comforted by God.
For just as the sufferings of Christ abound in us, so also our comfort abounds through Christ.
If we are afflicted, it is for your comfort and salvation; and if we are comforted, it is for your comfort, which is made effective through endurance of the same sufferings that we also suffer.
And our hope for you is firm, because we know that just as we share in the sufferings, so also we share in the comfort.
For I do not want you to be unaware, brothers, of the trouble we experienced in Asia: we were weighed down far beyond our strength, so that we despaired even of life.
Indeed, we ourselves received the sentence of death within ourselves, so that we would not rely on ourselves but on God, who raises the dead.
He rescued us from such a death, and he will rescue us.

For we have set our hope on him that he will rescue us again, with the help of your prayers for us, so that many may offer abundant thanksgiving on our behalf for the gracious gifts bestowed on us through many people.

For this is our boast, the testimony of our conscience: that we have conducted ourselves in the world with holiness and godly sincerity, not with fleshly wisdom but with the grace of God, and especially toward you.
For we write nothing else to you except what you read and understand, and I hope that you will understand to the end,
just as you have understood us in part: that we are your boast, just as you are ours, on the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.
With this confidence, I intended to come to you first, so that you might receive a second blessing,
and to go from you to Macedonia, and then to return from Macedonia to you and be sent on by you to Judea.
When I planned this, did I act lightly? Or do I make my plans according to the flesh, so that on my part “Yes” should be “Yes” and “No” should be “No”?
God is faithful: our word that came to you is not “Yes” and “No.”
For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, who was preached among you by us—by me, Silvanus, and Timothy—was not “Yes” and “No,” but in him there was “Yes.”
For however many promises God has made, in him is the “Yes.” Therefore, through him also comes the “Amen” spoken by us to the glory of God.
But it is God who established us, together with [?], in Christ and anointed us.
He also sealed us and gave the Spirit in our hearts as a pledge.

But I call God as a witness concerning my soul that it was to spare you that I did not come again to Corinth. Not that we rule over your faith, but we are fellow workers in the grace you have received, for you stand firm by faith.
But I decided this: not to come to you again in sorrow.
For if I make you sorrowful, who is there to make me glad except those who are made sorrowful by me?
And I wrote this so that, when I came, I would not suffer sorrow from those who ought to make me glad. I am confident in all of you that my joy is the joy of you all.
For out of much distress and anguish of heart I wrote to you with many tears, not to make you sorrowful, but so that you might know the especially great love I have for you.
But if anyone has caused sorrow, he has caused sorrow not to me, but to some extent—to avoid putting it too heavily—to all of you.
The punishment imposed by the majority is enough for such a person.
Now, on the contrary, you should forgive and comfort him, so that such a person is not overwhelmed by excessive sorrow.
Therefore I urge you to reaffirm your love for him.
For this very reason I also wrote, to test whether you would be obedient in everything.
If you forgive anyone, I do too. For if I forgive anything, what I forgive is for your sake in the presence of Christ.
So that Satan may not take advantage of us, for we are not ignorant of his schemes.
But when I came to Troas for the gospel of Christ, and a door was opened for me in the Lord,
I had no rest in my spirit, because I did not find Titus my brother there. Instead, I took leave of them and went to Macedonia.
But thanks be to God, who always leads us in triumph in Christ Jesus and through us makes the fragrance of his knowledge known everywhere.
For we are the sweet fragrance of Christ to God among those who are being saved and among those who are perishing.
To some, a fragrance from death to death, and to others, a fragrance from life to life. And who is sufficient for this?
For we are not like the others who peddle the word of God. Rather, we speak in Christ with sincerity, as people sent from God, in the presence of God.
Are we now beginning to commend ourselves again? Surely we do not need letters of recommendation to you or from you, as some do.
But you are our letters, written on our hearts, known and read by everyone.
You are clearly letters of Christ, delivered through our ministry, written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, not on stone tablets but on tablets of human hearts.
We have such a hope toward God through Christ.
Not that we are sufficient in ourselves to think of anything as coming from ourselves; rather, our sufficiency comes from God.
He has also made us sufficient to be ministers of these new covenants, not of the letter but of the spirit, for the letter kills, but the spirit gives life.

For if the ministry of death, engraved in letters on stone tablets, came with glory, so that the children of Israel could not look at Moses’ face because of the glory of his face, which was to pass away,
how much more will the ministry of the Spirit be glorious!
For if the ministry of condemnation was glorious, how much more glorious is the ministry of righteousness!
Indeed, what was glorified has no glory in this respect, because of the surpassing glory.
For if what was to pass away was glorious, how much more will what is to come be glorious!
Therefore, since we have such a hope, let us act with great boldness,
and not as Moses did, putting a veil over his face so that the children of Israel would not look at the end of what was passing away.
But their minds were blinded, for to this day the same veil remains over the reading of the old covenant and is not lifted, because it will be done away with in Christ.
But to this day, whenever they read Moses, the same veil lies over their hearts.
But when they turn to the Lord, then the veil will be lifted.
For the Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom.
But all of us, with unveiled faces, seeing the glory of the Lord as in a mirror, are being renewed into the same image, from glory to glory, as by the Spirit of the Lord.
Therefore, having this ministry, just as we have received mercy, we do not lose heart.
But we have renounced shameful secrets, so that we may not walk in cunning or falsify the word of God, but by making the truth known may commend ourselves to every human conscience before God.
But even if our gospel is veiled, it is veiled among those who are perishing.
The god of this world has blinded the minds of these unbelievers, so that the light of the gospel of the glory of Christ, who is the image of the invisible God, may not shine upon them.
For we do not preach ourselves, but Jesus Christ as Lord, and ourselves as your servants for Christ’s sake.
For God, who said that light should shine out of darkness, has himself shone in our hearts to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.
Now we have this treasure in earthen vessels, so that the surpassing power may be from God and not from us.
We are afflicted in every way, but not overcome; in need, but not in despair;
persecuted, but not abandoned; tormented, but not destroyed.
At all times we carry the death of Jesus in our bodies, so that the life of Jesus may also be revealed in our bodies.
For we who are alive are always being handed over to death for Jesus’ sake, so that the life of Jesus may also be revealed in our mortal bodies.
Thus death is at work in us, and life in you.
Now we have the same spirit of faith, as it is written: “I believed, therefore I spoke.” We too believe, and therefore we also speak.
We know this: that the one who raised Jesus will also raise us with Jesus and present us together with [?].
For everything is for your sake, so that grace, abounding through the thanksgiving of many, may increase to the glory of God.
Therefore we do not lose heart. Even though our outer person is wasting away, our inner person is being renewed day by day.
For the momentary abundance of our light affliction produces in us an eternally surpassing greatness of glory.
For we do not know the things that are visible, but the things that are invisible; for visible things last only a time, but invisible things are eternal.
For we know that if the earthly house in which we dwell is dismantled, we have a building from God, a house not made by hands, eternal in the heavens.
And over this we groan, for we long to clothe ourselves with our dwelling from heaven.
Provided that, when we put it on, we are not found naked.

For while we are in this dwelling, we groan under our burden, because we do not want to be stripped of it, but to put the other dwelling on over it, so that what is mortal may be swallowed up by life.
Now it is God who prepares us for this very thing, and he has given us the Spirit as a pledge.
So we are always confident and know that as long as we remain here in the body, we are away from the Lord.
For we walk by faith, not by appearances.
But we are confident, and would much rather leave this body and enter God's presence.
Therefore we make every effort to be pleasing to him, whether we remain here or depart.
For we must all appear before Christ's judgment seat, so that each may receive in his own body what is due for whatever he previously did, whether good or evil.
Now, knowing the fear of the Lord, we seek to win people's minds over to some extent. But we are plainly known to God, and I hope that we are plainly known in your minds as well.
We are not commending ourselves to you again, but giving you a reason to boast about us, so that you may have an answer for those who boast about outward appearances and not about the heart.
For if we have been out of our minds, that is for God; and if we are in our right minds, that is for you.
For Christ's love compels us to consider this: if one died in place of all, then all were dead.
And he died for all, so that those who live should no longer live for themselves, but for him who died for them and rose again.
From now on, we know no one according to the flesh. Even though we once knew Christ according to the flesh, we no longer know him in that way.
But if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation, for the old has passed away, and now everything has become new.
And everything is from God, who reconciled us to himself through Christ and gave us the ministry of reconciliation.
For God was reconciling the world to himself through Christ, not counting their sins against them, and he entrusted the message of reconciliation to us.
Therefore we serve as ambassadors for Christ, as though God were making his appeal through us. We plead on Christ's behalf: be reconciled to God.
For he made the one who knew no sin to be sin for our sake, so that through him we might become the righteousness of God.
We are your fellow workers, and we urge you not to receive God's grace in vain.
For he says, “At an acceptable time I heard you, and on the day of salvation I helped you.” Look, now is the acceptable time; look, now is the day of salvation.
Do not give any cause for offense in anything, so that the ministry may not be discredited.
Instead, in everything commend yourselves as servants of God, with great endurance in afflictions, in distress, in suffering,
in beatings, in imprisonments, in disturbances, in hard work, in sleepless nights, in fasts,
in purity, in knowledge, in patience, in kindness, in the Holy Spirit, in love without hypocrisy,
in words of truth, in the power of God, through the weapons of righteousness on the right and on the left.
Through glory and dishonor, praise and reproach; regarded as deceivers, yet truthful.
As unknown, yet known; as dying, and yet here we are, alive; as disciplined, yet not condemned to death.
As sorrowful, yet always rejoicing; as poor, yet making many rich; as having nothing, yet possessing everything.
Our mouths are open to you, Corinthians, and our hearts are wide open.
You are not constrained by us, but you are constrained in your own affections.
Now, in return—I address you as children—open your hearts wide too.
Do not be yoked together with unbelievers. For what partnership does righteousness have with lawlessness? Or what does light have in common with darkness?
Or what agreement is there between Christ and Beliar?

Or what share does a believer have with an unbeliever? Or what likeness is there between God's temple and pagan temples? For you are the temple of the living God, as God said: “I will dwell among them and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they will be my people.”
Therefore, come out from among them and separate yourselves, says the Lord, and do not touch unclean things.
And I will receive you, and I will be a Father to you, and you will be sons and daughters to me, says the Lord Almighty.
Since we have this good news, beloved, let us cleanse ourselves of every defilement of body and spirit, bringing holiness to completion in the fear of God.
Bear with us, for we have wronged no one, corrupted no one, and deprived no one of anything.
I do not say this to condemn you, for I have already said that you are in our hearts, to live and die with you.
I have great confidence in you and take great pride in you. I am filled with comfort and overflowing with joy in all our troubles.
For when we arrived in Macedonia, our bodies found no rest at all. Instead, we were troubled in every way: conflicts outside and terrors within.
But God, who comforts the lowly, comforted us through the arrival of Titus.
Not only through his arrival, but also through the comfort he received from you, as he told us of your longing, your mourning, and your zeal for me, so that I rejoiced all the more.
For even if I made you sorrowful with that letter, I do not regret it, though I did regret it. For I see that the letter made you sorrowful, even if only for a while.
Now I rejoice, not because you were sorrowful, but because your sorrow led to repentance. For you were sorrowful in accordance with God, so that you suffered no harm from us in anything.
For sorrow in accordance with God produces repentance leading to salvation, without regret, but the sorrow of the world produces death.

Now this very thing, that you grieved according to God's will—what diligence it produced in you, what appeals, what indignation, what fear, what longing, what zeal, what desire for justice! For in everything you showed yourselves to be innocent in this matter.

So even though I wrote to you, it was not for the sake of the one who did wrong, nor for the sake of the one who was wronged, but so that your earnest concern for us might become clear to you before God.
For this reason we have been comforted. In addition to our comfort, we rejoiced still more at Titus's joy, because his spirit had been refreshed by all of you.
For whatever I boasted to him about you, I was not put to shame. But just as everything we said to you was true, so our boasting to Titus also proved true.
And his affection for you is even greater, for he reminded us of the obedience of all of you, and how you received him with fear and trembling.
And now I rejoice that I have confidence in you in everything.
Brothers, I make known to you the grace of God that has been given to the churches of Macedonia.
For in a great ordeal of affliction, their overflowing joy and their deep poverty abounded in a wealth of generosity.
For I testify that they gave according to their ability, and even beyond their ability, of their own accord.
With many pleas they begged to give us the gift and their contribution to the service for the saints.
And not merely as we had expected: they gave themselves first to the Lord and then to us, by the will of God.
We urged Titus that, just as he had begun earlier, he should also complete this act of grace among you.
But just as you excel in everything—in faith, speech, knowledge, all diligence, and the love that comes from us to you—see that you also excel in this act of grace.
I do not say this as a command, but through the diligence of others I am testing the sincerity of your love.
For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ: though he was rich, he became poor for your sake, so that through his poverty you might become rich.
And I give advice in this matter, for this is beneficial to you, who began last year not only to do this but also to desire it.
But now complete the deed itself, so that just as you were willing and eager, you may also carry it out according to what you have.
For if willingness is present, it is acceptable according to what one has, not according to what one does not have.
For I do not wish relief for others and hardship for you,
but equality: at the present time, your abundance should supply their need, so that their abundance may also supply your need, and there may be equality, as it is written:
“The one who gathered much had no excess, and the one who gathered little had no shortage.”
But thanks be to God, who put the same concern for you into the heart of Titus.
For he accepted our appeal and, being still more eager, willingly undertook to come to you.
And we sent with him the brother whose praise in the gospel is known throughout all the churches.
And not only that: he was also appointed by the churches to be our traveling companion in this gracious gift, which we administer for the glory of the Lord and to show our willingness.
But we were careful about this, lest anyone find fault with us concerning this substantial gift administered by us.
For we take thought for what is good, not only before the Lord but also before people.
And we sent with them our brother, whom we have tested in many matters and often found steadfast, and who is now even more steadfast because of his great confidence in you.
If there is any question about Titus, he is my partner and your fellow worker; and as for our brothers, they are messengers of the church and the glory of Christ.
Therefore show them the proof of your love and of our boasting about you, before all the churches.
Now concerning the service for the saints, it is unnecessary for me even to write to you.
For I know your eagerness, about which I have boasted to the Macedonians, saying that the people of Achaia have been ready since last year; and your zeal has stirred up many.
And we sent the brothers so that our boasting about you might not prove empty in this matter, but that you might be found fully prepared, just as I said.
Otherwise, if Macedonians come with us and find you unprepared, we—not to mention you—will be put to shame in this matter of boasting.
So I considered it necessary to urge the brothers to come to you beforehand and prepare in advance your previously promised gift, so that it would be ready as a blessing and not as an act of greed.
For this is so: whoever sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and whoever sows generously will also reap generously.
Let each person give as willingly decided in the heart, not under compulsion or with sorrow, for God loves cheerful, generous gifts.
But God is able to make every grace abound toward you, so that, always having everything you need in every respect, you may abound in every good work.
As it is also written: “He scattered his gifts and gave to the poor; his righteousness remains forever.”
May he who supplies seed to sowers and bread for food supply and multiply your seed and increase the fruits of your righteousness.
You are enriched in everything for every kind of generosity, which produces thanksgiving to God through us.
For the service of this contribution not only supplies what the saints lack, but also overflows in many expressions of thanksgiving to God.
Through the proof given by this service, they glorify God for the obedience of your confession to the gospel of Christ and for your generous sharing with them and with everyone.
And their prayers are for you, because they long for you on account of the surpassing grace of God that is in you.
But thanks be to God for his indescribable gifts!
Now I, Paul myself, appeal to you by the gentleness and kindness of Christ—I who am humble among you when present, but bold toward you when far away.
I beg you that, when I am present, I may not have to be bold with the confidence with which I intend to confront certain people who think that we conduct ourselves according to the flesh.
For although we live in the flesh, we do not wage war according to the flesh.
For the weapons of our warfare are not of the flesh, but are powerful through God for tearing down strongholds.
We tear down arguments and every lofty thing that rises proudly against the knowledge of God, and we take every thought captive into obedience to Christ.
And we are ready to punish every act of disobedience when your obedience too is complete.
Look at what is before your eyes. If anyone is confident that he belongs to Christ, let him consider again in his own mind that, just as he belongs to Christ, so do we.
For even if I boast still more about our authority, which the Lord gave us to build you up and not to tear you down, I will not be ashamed.
I do not want to seem as though I am frightening you with my letters.
They say, “His letters are weighty and severe, but his bodily presence is weak and his speech is contemptible.”
Let such a person consider this: what we are in the words of our letters when far away, we will also be in our actions when present.

For we do not dare to compare or equate ourselves with some who commend themselves to you. But when they measure themselves by themselves and compare themselves with themselves, they do not understand.
But we will not boast beyond measure, only within the limits of the sphere God allotted to us—a sphere that reaches as far as you.
We are not overextending ourselves as though we had not reached you, for we came as far as you with the gospel of Christ.
Nor do we boast beyond measure in the labors of others. But we have hope that, as your faith grows, we will be greatly enlarged among you within our allotted sphere.
Then we may preach the gospel beyond you, without boasting of work already done within someone else’s sphere.
For whoever boasts, let him boast in the Lord.
For it is not the one who commends himself who is approved, but the one whom the Lord commends.
It would be good if you would bear with a little of my foolishness. Indeed, do bear with me.
I stir you to jealousy with God's jealousy, for I have betrothed you to one husband, to present you to Christ as a pure virgin.
But I fear that, just as the serpent deceived Eve by his cunning, your minds may be corrupted and led away from your sincerity toward Christ.

For if someone comes and preaches another Christ whom we did not preach, or you receive a different spirit which you did not receive, or a different gospel which you did not accept, you bear with them readily.
But I consider myself in no way inferior to the foremost apostles.
Even if I am unskilled in speech, I am not unskilled in knowledge. In every respect we have made ourselves fully known to you.
Did I commit any offense by humbling myself so that you might be exalted, because I preached God's gospel to you free of charge?
I robbed other churches, taking wages from them to serve you.

When I came to you, although I lacked something, I did not burden any of you, for the brothers who came from Macedonia supplied what I lacked. In every way I kept myself from being a burden to you, and I will continue to do so.
As the truth of Christ is in me, this boasting of mine will not be stopped in the regions of Achaia.
Why? As though I do not love you? God knows that I do.
What I am doing I will continue to do, so that I may cut off the opportunity of those who want an opportunity to be found equal to us in what they boast about.
For such people are false apostles, deceitful workers who disguise themselves as apostles of Christ.
And this is no wonder, for Satan himself disguises himself as an angel of light.
So it is no great thing if his servants also disguise themselves as servants of righteousness. Their end will be according to their deeds.
Again I say, let no one consider me a fool. But if you do, at least receive me as a fool, so that I too may boast a little.
What I am saying, I do not say according to the Lord, but as though in foolishness, in this manner of boasting.
Since many boast according to the flesh, I too will boast.
You readily put up with fools in your wisdom.

For you bear with anyone who deceives you, anyone who enslaves you, anyone who consumes your possessions, anyone who takes something from you, anyone who acts arrogantly, or anyone who strikes you in the face.
I say this with shame, as though we had been weak. Yet whatever anyone dares to do—I speak in foolishness—I too dare to do.
Are they Hebrews? So am I. Are they Israelites? So am I. Are they descendants of Abraham? So am I.
Are they servants of Christ? I will speak even more recklessly: I am more so—in greater labors, in still more beatings, in imprisonment more than they, and in facing death many times.
Five times I received forty lashes less one from the Jews.
Three times I was beaten with rods, once I was stoned, three times I was shipwrecked, and I suffered a day and a night in the depths.

On frequent journeys, I faced troubles from rivers, troubles from robbers, troubles from my own people, troubles from Gentiles, troubles in the city, troubles in the wilderness, troubles at sea, and troubles from false brothers.
I endured toil and labor, frequent sleeplessness, hunger and thirst, frequent fasting, cold and nakedness.
Leaving aside the other hardships, the crowd pressed upon me every day, and I bore the care of all the churches.
Who is weak, and I am not weak? Who stumbles, and I do not burn with distress?
If I must boast, I will boast of my weakness.
The God and Father of our Lord Jesus, who is blessed forever, knows that I am not lying.
In Damascus, the governor under King Aretas was guarding the city of the Damascenes to seize me.
I was lowered in a basket through a window in the wall and escaped from his hands.
Now I must boast, though it does no good. But I will come to visions and revelations of the Lord.
I know a man in Christ who fourteen years ago was caught up to the third heaven. Whether in the body I do not know, or outside the body I do not know; God knows.
And I know that man—whether in the body or outside the body I do not know; God knows—
that he was caught up into paradise and heard inexpressible words that a person is not permitted to speak.
I will boast about such a person, but I will not boast about myself except in my weaknesses.
For even if I wished to boast, I would not be a fool, because I would be speaking the truth. But I refrain, lest anyone think more of me than what they see in me or hear from me.
And so that I would not become proud because of the extraordinary revelations, I was given a thorn in the flesh, a messenger of Satan to strike me, so that I would not become proud.
Because of this, I pleaded with the Lord three times to take it away from me.
And he said to me, “My grace is enough for you, for my power is perfected in weakness.” So it is all the better for me to boast in my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may dwell in me.
Therefore I am content with weaknesses, insults, troubles, persecutions, and hardships for Christ’s sake. For when I am weak, then I am strong.
I became a fool, because you forced me. For I ought to have received commendation from you, since I was found in no way inferior to the most eminent apostles, even though I am nothing.
Yet the signs of an apostle were performed among you with all patience, through signs, wonders, and mighty deeds.
Now in what way were you found inferior to the other churches, except that I did not burden you? Forgive me this wrong!

Look, this is the third time I am ready to come to you, and I will not be a burden to you, because I seek not what is yours but you. For children ought not to save up for their parents, but parents for their children.
But I will gladly spend and be spent for your souls, even if, in loving you more, I am loved less.
But admittedly I did not burden you. Yet, being crafty, I caught you by cunning!
Did I take advantage of you through any of those they sent to you?
I urged Titus and sent the brother with him. Did Titus take advantage of what was yours? Did we not walk in the same spirit? Did we not follow the same footsteps?
Do you again suppose that we are pleading with you through flattery? We speak before God in Christ, and everything, beloved, is for building you up.

But I fear that when I come, I may not find you as I wish, and you may find me as you do not wish. I fear there may again be strife, jealousy, anger, provocations, slander, whispering, pride, arrogance, and disorder.
Lest, when I come again, my God humble me before you, and I mourn for many who sinned before and have not repented of the impurity, sexual immorality, and lust they practiced.
This is the third time I am coming to you, so that every matter may be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses.
I warned you before, and I warn you again, having been present twice. Now I write from afar to those who sinned before and to all the others: if I come again, I will not spare anyone.
If you seek proof of Christ, who speaks to you through me, he is powerful among you, not weak.
For although he was crucified through our weakness, he lives by the power of God. And although we are weak because of him, we will live with him by the power of God.
Test yourselves to see whether you remain in the same faith; examine yourselves. Do you not know that Jesus Christ is in you—unless you fail the test?
But I hope you will know that we have not failed the test.
But we ask God that he do you no harm—not so that we may appear approved, but so that you may do what is good, even if we are found unfit.
For we can do nothing against the truth; rather, we are guardians of the truth.
We rejoice when we are weak and you are strong. This is precisely what we pray for: that you may be firmly established.
For this reason I write these things from afar, so that when I come I may not act harshly according to the authority the Lord gave me for building up and not for tearing down.
Finally, brothers, farewell. Stand firm, be comforted, be of one mind, and live in peace; and the God of peace and love will be with you.
Greet one another with a holy kiss. All the saints greet you.

The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with you all. Amen. The second letter to the Corinthians was written from Philippi through Titus and Luke.
